headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared filesystem/MCP; no evidence of direct compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while plano consumes config and OpenAI-compatible chat inputs; the pair can be bridged through shared files or copied outputs. That makes instruction-hijacking plausible in default developer workflows, though not proven by docs. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Continue writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that plano later parses as instructions
IF an MCP server or file bridge passes raw model output from Continue into plano without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the tools for untrusted content.
Require a human review step before plano consumes Continue-generated text.
Use separate directories for each agent's inputs and outputs.
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from file content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent file transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, open editor buffers, and workspace files; plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml. A shared filesystem or copied artifacts can move sensitive code or operational data between them, and both have broad network egress. The leakage path is plausible in default setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory
IF Continue or plano uploads file contents from that shared location to its backend
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace directory.
Remove secrets and logs from any shared folder before use.
Turn off automatic file ingestion for either agent where possible.
Use local-only models for Continue when handling sensitive code.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level directory isolation or sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad egress; plano has broad egress and an OpenAI-compatible API surface. They do not both advertise unrestricted writes to the same mutable resource, but shared filesystem state via Continue plus plano config files creates overlapping mutation risk. Because locking is undocumented, choose medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to edit the same repository or config tree
IF either agent writes while the other reads without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a distinct writable directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same file set.
Serialize runs when both touch shared artifacts.
Keep plano config read-only during Continue sessions.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or file edits that plano may later ingest as configuration or operational input, and plano exposes an API-routing layer that could act on those inputs. There is no documented verification boundary between them, so A's output can become B's input with no guardrail. That is a default-path medium risk.
conditions: IF plano consumes Continue-produced text as authoritative configuration or routing input
IF no human or automated verification step checks Continue output before plano acts on it
mitigations: Require validation before plano uses any Continue-generated artifact.
Keep Continue outputs in draft-only folders.
Add a checksum or schema check before downstream use.
Have a human approve any config or code emitted by Continue.
requires-engineering: implement typed interfaces between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Continue handles model-provider API keys and workspace code; plano handles logs and metrics, but the profiles do not show a regulated-data transfer or a jurisdictional conflict. With no evidence of a compliance breach, only a low residual gap remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent without an external policy review
IF a deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Review retention settings before deployment.
Document where logs and traces are stored.
Use separate tenants for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
